system.biography: A creature often confused with the chimera of Northi. Despite a similar appearance, the original minotaur is a cursed creature once locked away in a labyrinth. Its offspring now roam the world, causing destruction wherever they go.

details.appearance: A creature with the body of a man and the head of a bull.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the world.

system.tactics: The minotaur will use all their AP on Goring Charge if not in range of an enemy. Once in range, they will attack normally and use Headbutt when they can.
system.runningMonster: A group of minotaurs provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Its stats are fairly high, but its abilities are unimpressive and it mostly just basic attacks.

system.biography: Priests are spellcasters that draw their power from the gods. Due to the popularity and strength of Kari, the human goddess, the vast majority of priests in the world are human. However, priests of other races do still exist. Some may follow Kari, while others may follow their own god or goddess.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics:
A priest will want to play close to the frontlines to be in range for Angel’s Embrace. Once the melee’s of each side have engaged on combat, the priest can drop a hallowed ground in such a way that it affects all of their melee allies. Afterwards, they will focus on attacking and will use their remaining mana to cast Cure Touch once an ally (heroic allies only if there is any left) becomes low on HP.

Angel’s Embrace can be used to absorb big hits on allies, though the priest should stop using it unless to prevent a killing blow once their own RP becomes too low.
system.runningMonster:
Priests are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being both a support and healer. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Acolyte’ generic enemy.

Priests can function with Grunt level allies, though their support will not be nearly as effective as when supporting heroic allies. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Priests can use either a channeling weapon or a light melee weapon + shield. Priests can wear anything from no armor, light armor to medium armor. In the stat block above, a light melee weapon + shield and light armor is assumed.

system.description: Your Healing spells do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

system.biography:
The raiju is often confused for an animal due to its appearance. In reality, its an elemental that serves as the hunting dog for a more powerful elemental creature. It will track and hound an enemy from afar, then move in for the kill once the weather changes.

Storms have an unnaturally high chance of appearing when this creature is around.

details.appearance: A white wolf like creature around which electricity constantly crackles.
details.habitat: Rarely found anywhere in the wild. Only seen by those it is hunting.

system.tactics:
The Raiju's strategy is the same regardless of whether its storming or not. It will start by using Static Field at encounter start.

On its turn, it will use Static Charge to pass through as many enemies as it can, without having to move before using Lightning Charge. The remaining AP will be used on attacking.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of Raiju will provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. During a storm, you'll want to lower the amount if you want to keep the difficulty similar as the same group of Raiju can quickly murder a group of low level adventurers.

If it is hunting one of the party members, you can have the Raiju focus on that party member even at risk to themselves.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hide.

system.description: You take no damage from Lightning damage.
Your Focus, Power and Agility are doubled during a storm.

system.biography: Rogues are shifty individuals that use trickery and dirty tactics to win battles. They exist in every race and society.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: Rogues aim for the backline, targeting enemy mages or archers. They can slip past the frontlines using Feint and can avoid enemy attacks by using their 0 RP evasive maneuver. If an enemy is at 0 RP, they can move to that enemy and use their Devastating Strike on them.
system.runningMonster:
Rogue are intended to be generic grunt enemies that focus on skirmishing. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Assassin’ generic enemy.

Rogues can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Rogues prefer light or no armor along with a pair of light weapons, usually daggers.

system.biography: These creatures are created by skilled necromancers and due to their regenerative abilities will often out live their masters. Though they are mindless, their former instructions still linger and they are likely to attack any creatures that approach it.

details.appearance: A large skeletal creature that has 2 pairs of extra arms. It sits low to the floor and uses one of the pairs of arms to support its weight. Despite this, it still towers above the average person. Their frontal arms are sharpened into blades instead of having hands.
details.habitat: Usually found in places a necromancer has been.

system.tactics:
The Skeletal Monstrosity’s battle strategy is simple. It will attack a random target (or the target that did the most damage to it the previous round) and use Skeletal Armblade Barrage. Afterwards, it will use the sweep against the largest group of targets. After those two attacks, it will keep making light and heavy attacks as appropriate.

If there are no enemies in his attack range, which is 10ft, it will use Bone Spike Shot until an enemy is pulled within its range, then continue with the above mentioned strategy.
system.runningMonster:
The Skeletal Monstrosity is a good enemy to face by itself. Against stronger parties, you can add a few normal skeletons to the mix or give the creature additional arms to further boost its action economy.

Token wise, you want to have a bigger token for the main body (10x10ft token) and then 4 5x5ft tokens for each of the arms. The arms should be adjacent to the main body in some way.

system.description: You have 4 arms which can be targeted separately from the main body. For each active arm, you gain 1 AP. Each arm has 40 HP and uses the Dodge and Guard of the main body. They have 1 RP, which regenerates at the start of your turn. Each arm is attached to the main body and moves along with it. They otherwise have a movement speed of 0 and are immune to Knockbacks, Prone and other disabling effects. An AoE attack only does damage to 1 part of your body, either the main body or an arm, which is chosen by the attacker.
Each of your individual parts regenerates Toughness HP at the start of your turn. This continues even after a body part reaches 0 HP until all body parts have been reduced to 0 HP or lower.
Your attacks can attack targets up to 10ft away.
You are immune to all mind-affecting effects.

system.biography: Sniper is a title given to all users of ranged weaponry that display some level of skill. They exist in every race and can use a wide variety of ranged weapons.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics:
The sniper’s strategy in combat is to sit still as far away as possible and do damage to the most vulnerable target. What the most vulnerable target is may change during the course of the battle and a sniper can easily adapt to the situation.

They can use Homing Shot when dealing with high dodge characters. If they are engaged in melee combat, they will use Disengaging Shot if they have mana for it. If they don’t, the common strategy is to switch to a melee weapon.
system.runningMonster:
Snipers are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on ranged combat. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Archer’ generic enemy.

Snipers can be run together with several grunt level enemies or in a group together with around 3 similar heroic enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Snipers can use any type of ranged weapon, though pistols, shotguns and sniper rifles are rarely seen. Snipers often wear no or light armor. Most will also carry a melee weapon as a backup weapon.

system.biography: Tacticians are found in virtually every society and can be of any race. Oftentimes, but not always, they are leaders such as a captain, general or something simpler like a bandit chief. They lead their troops to victory not always through charisma, but through tactics.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: The tactician relies mostly on their troops to do the damage. Their job is to apply Focus Fire to the target most vulnerable or which is reachable by the most of their troops. They can use reposition to cut off escapes or make their allies easily reach the backline. They will always use Stratagem: Lightning at the start of the encounter.
system.runningMonster:
Tacticians are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on tactics and leadership. They can easily be used for any race or situation that requires it.

A tactician is worthless without a good number of grunt level allies. They can pair well with both melee attackers with Stratagem: Lightning and Reposition, but also ranged attackers due to easier Focus Fire usage.

With Battle Tactics, you are free to play the enemies as smartly as you can, roleplaying it as the tactician giving precise orders. Tacticians can use a wide variety of weapons and armor depending on the race or society they are from. Ranged weapons are generally preferable, as a tactician going down may lead to an instant loss.

official.notableSkills: Knowledge History+11, Perception+10, Negotiation+11, Intimidation+11, Deception+10

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: The tank’s strategy is to move up to take space, then provoke the closest melee enemy he can.

Tank can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Trolls descend from what were once regular humans that mutated into these hideous creatures. 

In a way, they are similar to what hobgoblins are to normal goblins. Perhaps because of this, they are often found in the company of them.

system.biography: Unstable Efreets are split off parts of a normal Efreet. Their very existence is a fleeting thing with them being able to exist for little more than day before their flames going out and them vanishing into nothingness.

details.appearance: A creature of pure fire and flame that appears roughly in a humanoid shape.

system.tactics: Unstable Efreet’s strategy is very simple. They will run towards the nearest enemy and attack them until they die and explode.
system.runningMonster: For the most effective use, Unstable Efreets should not start too far away from the players, otherwise they might cause a chain reaction of explosions before they get in range. Be careful when putting these against a Pyromancer. Pyromancers can trivialize this encounter by tagging them with fire spells, but if they do it while the Unstable Efreets are too close, then they could cause a chain reaction that leads to a constant barrage of explosions on the players.

system.description: When your HP is lowered to 0, you will immediately use Explode Self as a reaction. After that, you immediately die.
When you take fire damage, you will start to explode. At the end of your next turn, your HP will be set to 0 and you will use Explode Self.
You take half damage from all fire damage and your attacks deal fire damage.

system.biography: Warriors are combatants that specialize in melee combat. They exist in every race and civilization and can use a wide variety of weapons and armor.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: Warriors use Charge to engage the frontline in combat and hit the most vulnerable target there. If engaged with two or more enemies, they will use Cleaving Strike. Else, they will use Skullsplitter if the target is wearing at least medium armor.
system.runningMonster:
Warriors are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being a hardhitting melee. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Brute’ generic enemy.

Warriors can function with Grunt level allies, but they will want some tank type allies to not get focused down as hard. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Warriors generally use heavy melee weapons. They can use no armor, light armor or medium armor depending on the race. The stat block above assumes light armor and a heavy melee weapon. Some might carry a ranged weapon as backup.

Heavy Paladins are intelligent creatures and veteran fighters. Don't be afraid to play them intelligently. If a paladin can hit a demon in their divine release state with their divine smite, they should always do so unless it would cause them to provoke too many attacks.

system.biography: When a creature is slain by a Wraith, there's a high chance a Wight will be born from its corpse. Wights are automatically subservient to the Wraith that killed them and must stay within a mile radius of it or disappear entirely.

details.habitat: Appears around places where a Wraith is.

system.tactics: The wight will attacks the closest target. It can choose between Spectral Touch or Draining Touch + a light attack, both are valid options.
system.runningMonster:
Wights are very strong against physical attackers. Even a small group of wights can be annoying to fight when you don't have any non-physical damage. Consider the party's abilities very carefully when choosing how many wights to put in.

You can choose to have Wights use their RP immediately, which opens them up for physical attackers, or have them save their RP so they can always react to the physical attackers. The first option will make the fight more manageable for the party members who don't have magical damage options.

system.biography: A vengeful spirit that died in the darkness while it was still alive. Brought back to life through a necromancer or through astra corruption, they attack any living creature that they can see. They are weak to bright lights and will never willingly go into the sunlight.

details.appearance: A translucent dark creature with a vaguely humanoid shape.
details.habitat: Found only in permanently dark places.

system.tactics:
The Wraith will avoid bright light the best it can, only going in if it has no other choice. It may use Darkness in this case to negate the effects of it if possible.

If it doesn't need to avoid bright light, it will use Darkness after spending 3 AP, then immediately follow up with Darkness Shade to hide.

For attacks, it will use the Spectral Touch and Draining Touch. Like other incorporeal enemies, it can freely react to any physical attacks without burning RP.
system.runningMonster:
A group of wraith's can provide a good challenge to a high spirit core party. At this point, most people should have a way of dealing non-physical weapon. The wraith's stats are a bit higher than the other incorporeal enemies, so be careful because some members of the party may have 0 chance of hitting it even with that.

Having a source of bright light also helps the players. A torch alone wouldn't qualify, but a northi lantern or a paladin's holy weapon might.

You do not spend your RP when reacting against a physical attack made with a non-magical weapon. A weapon that is enchanted counts as magical.
If you are in an area with a bright light, become Weakened.
You may move through solid objects and enemies with no penalty.

system.biography: A distant relative of the dragons that have vanished. Though they spent most of their time sleeping in their caves, they are hostile to all living creatures and view them are little more than prey. Wyrms are older, more intelligent and more dangerous than their Drake and Wyrmling counterparts.

details.appearance: A large scaled lizard with a pair of wings on its back.
details.habitat: Most commonly found high in the mountain in places with a warm temperature.

system.tactics:
The firewyrm will rain fire from the sky until it is forced down to the ground or it runs out of mana. Even when out of mana, it may still choose to do fly-by attacks instead of staying on the ground.

While in the sky, it can use both Fireball and Flame Breath at the largest group of enemies. On the ground, it will use tail swipe as the final action of each round and may still use flame breath if it has mana left.

At the encounter start, it will always use Terrifying Roar.
system.runningMonster:
The firewyrm is a solo monster that is a serious threat to any party without aeromancers. In a space where their flight is limited, they can be less threatening. As they are intelligent creatures, a firewyrm may retreat if the battle starts going badly for it.

The firewyrm is bigger than a drake, but the token size is still the same.

Gather Parts: 1000 units of dragonscale.

system.description: When you inflict Burning on a target that is already suffering from Burning, they immediately take Fire damage equal to the existing Burning value.
You take no damage from Fire damage.

You can fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so. While flying, you may make any of your attacks (spending AP as normal) during your movement and continue to move afterwards.
You gain +1 Guard, and a further +2 Guard when taking the Block action (Already added to stats).

system.biography: Mindless corpses resurrected through necromancy or astra corruption.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature with decaying skin.
details.habitat: Found in places with corpses or near necromancers.

system.tactics: Zombies move towards the near enemy. If the target is not already grabbed (by any zombie) and they can make a Heavy attack, they make a Heavy attack. Otherwise if they are not already grabbing an enemy, they will do so.
system.runningMonster: A large group of zombies is a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Zombies are weak to holy damage, so you will want to add more of them to keep the challenge the same when the players have classes like a paladin or priest with them. Zombies are slow, but relatively tanky for a grunt enemy. Against parties that are less likely to exploit this weakness or if fighting in a place where its impossible to do, you may want to use slightly less zombies.

system.description: You take double damage from Holy damage.
You are immune to all mind-affecting effects.
